newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM renews offer of talks with opponents.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM renews offer of talks with opponents.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday renewed an invitation to her main political foe and predecessor Begum Khaleda Zia for a live television debate on major national issues.

"I am still ready for a discussion or debate with her (Khaleda Zia). Let's together face people on the television. I don't have anything to hide," Hasina told a rally organised by ruling Awami League.
Hasina, facing mounting political tension, made a similar offer last week, but Khaleda turned it down, saying it would be "meaningless."

"Such a dialogue will be nothing but a mockery at this stage. They (government) have finished all preparations to put the nation's existence at stake," Khaleda, head of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), told a party meeting on Saturday.

She charged the government with endangering Bangladesh's sovereignty and independence by striking what she termed were "secret deals" with India, and called for united resistance by "nationalist forces".
Those who quickly responded to Khaleda's call included the fundamentalist Jamaat-e-Islami and radical Jatiya ganatantrik Party, known for their staunch anti-Indian stance.

Hasina, who took office in June after her Awami League defeated BNP in general elections, said all her programmes were aimed at development of the impoverished country, and cautioned people against opposition propaganda.
"Be vigilant against on-going conspiracy to foil the economic progress," Hasina said repeating the allegation that the BNP was sabotaging her development efforts.
The Prime Minister said her government was receiving "tremendous response" from foreign investors with the country's image fast improving.
"Investments are coming and will continue to come," said a confident-looking Hasina with visiting Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer sitting beside her on the dais.

Fischer, who arrived in Dhaka earlier on Monday for a three-day official, also spoke at the rally, giving the audience a rare opportunity to listen to a foreign dignitary addressing a political rally.
People cheered and clapped as Fishcer pledged Australian cooperation to Bangladesh's development efforts, and presented Hasina with a signed cricket bat.
The presentation symbolised Bangladesh's prospect of playing in the cricket World Cup, officials said. Bangladesh is a favourite to qualify for the World Cup.
